pages.sceneDescription:
On a foggy autumn morning along the wide paved stone quay below the Grossmünster, an adult man—Daniel, sporting dark brown wavy short hair, a short beard and mustache, brown eyes, wearing a green waxed-cotton hooded anorak zipped to mid-chest, a white cotton crew-neck underlayer, grey straight-leg denim jeans, and brown leather lace-up sneakers—lunges forward in the left foreground. He extends his right arm straight out, reaching desperately for a palm-sized wooden kite reel wrapped in red string that rises into the air just past his fingertips. Standing a few paces away in the midground, a preschool-age little girl and a young school-age boy watch the reel escape. The girl, Emma, has ear-length wavy brown hair in a right-parted ponytail, brown eyes, freckles, and wears her costumed outfit: a red and white striped cotton long-sleeve undershirt, black cotton calf-length trousers with ragged hems, a black cotton Piratentuch tied around her waist, brown leather ankle boots, and a red cotton bandana over her head. Beside her stands Noah, a young school-age boy with short curly light blonde hair and blue eyes, wearing his light blue top, dark grey trousers, and brown shoes. High in the background above the broad Limmat river, the thick autumn fog partially swallows a house-height wooden pirate ship with a tall central mast, and a pristine yellow paper kite flies up into the white mist toward it. In the far distance, a few small figures stroll along the quay, their coats muted against the grey stones. The wide shot captures the damp grey stones of the quay under the pale morning light, the twin stone cathedral towers looming faintly through the fog behind the autumn trees.

pages.sceneDescription:
From the perspective of the small wooden rowboat bobbing by the stone Wasserkirche, an elderly man—Hans, with short straight white hair, brown eyes, a prominent white mustache, stooped posture, wearing a grey wool flat cap, a yellow oilskin long coat with wide lapels over a white collared shirt, brown wool straight-leg trousers, and black rubber waterproof ankle boots—stands in the foreground gripping the boat's wooden gunwale, one hand wrapped around the worn timber, the other resting on the oar. In the midground, Emma and Noah climb down a long hemp rope ladder draped over the pirate ship's dark hull. Emma, with her brown ponytail and red bandana, red and white striped undershirt, black trousers and brown boots, grips a wooden rung with both hands, her feet resting on the rung below; Pepe, a melon-sized parrot with bright green body feathers, red tail feathers, blue wing tips and a curved black beak, perches on her right shoulder, his small black claws curling around the fabric of her shirt. Noah, with his blonde curls and blue eyes, wearing his orange life jacket over his light blue top and dark grey trousers, climbs beside her, his right hand gripping a rung and his left hand holding the paper kite—now ripped in two down the middle—against the ladder. A few distant figures walk along the embankment behind Hans. High in the background, Emma's black cotton Piratentuch flies from the ship's tall mast top in the last shreds of morning fog, catching the autumn wind as the ship departs.
